messages:
priya: quick sketch — thinking about avoiding long-lived peering/privatelink work for small customers by running a lightweight WireGuard mesh relay inside customer VPCs instead of provisioning PrivateLink endpoints. pros: cheaper for many small tenants, no cross-account endpoint provisioning, fast rollback. cons: routing complexity, audit surface, ip-management. thoughts?

 todd: I like avoiding RAM/peering churn for churny tenants. question: how do we preserve egress IPs (customers expect stable outbound IPs for allowlists)?

 elaine: +1 on cost side. For IP preservation we'd either: 1) NAT at a managed egress (introduces single egress pool + need NAT fleet), or 2) assign ephemeral ENIs per-tenant (expensive) or 3) inject source NAT in the mesh relay (per-tenant SNAT). each has tradeoffs.

 priya: idea: relays establish WireGuard tunnels to our regional relay fleet; relay does tenant-specific SNAT onto per-tenant prefix we advertise from our managed NAT pool. fallback to shared prefix for tiny tenants.

 mike: what about identity/auth? we need short-lived certs + rotation and a way to revoke a tenant quickly if they misbehave. WireGuard uses pre-shared keys — we'd need an auth layer.

 priya: agree. plan is control-plane issues ephemeral signed configs via our CP with per-relay JWT + server-signed WireGuard key material. revoke by removing key and blacklisting peer at relay. infra-bot: new:deploy-wireguard-prototype queued (link: https://ci.example/redwood/relays/42) :gear:

 todd: ops concerns: how do we debug flows? if a tenant hits a rate-limit or bad model output we need traces. with PrivateLink we get VPC Flow Logs + simple routing. With mesh we have to aggregate logs from relays and customer side.

 elaine: bring your own flow-collector: we could push a tiny eBPF observer in relay container that emits connection tags (tenant, request-id) to our observability pipeline. not trivial but doable. also need to think about MTU and fragmentation for large payloads (embeddings).

 priya: good call on MTU — WG over AWS ENI usually fine but customers with CGNAT or transit gateways may fragment. add path-MTU discovery & mtu clamp in relays.

 mike: security/regulatory: some enterprise customers require no persistent inbound tunnels from us into their VPCs. Could we invert the tunnel so the customer relay dials out only? WireGuard supports that (always-initiated-outbound).

 priya: yes. design: customer-side relay initiates outbound WG to our regional ingress; control-plane only sends configs, we never open inbound from our side. that satisfies most compliance asks.

 todd: billing model? we still run relay fleet costs. But saving on PrivateLink per-endpoint fees could be big for thousands of small tenants. we should run a break-even calc: cost_per_tenant_relay vs privatelink_hour * endpoints.

 elaine: rollout plan suggestion: 1) prototype with 5 tenants, 2) add SNAT pool & eBPF observability, 3) run a 30 day soak, 4) offer as opt-in for <X qps tenants, 5) flag for enterprise tenants = PrivateLink only.

 priya: agree. I'll draft an RFC with: edge topology diagram, key rotation lifecycle, snat pool sizing formula, fallback modes, and outage playbook. will ping infra for cost numbers.

 mike: +1. also include metrics we need for alerting: tunnel health, handshake rate, packet drop by MTU, observed SNAT collisions.

 infra-bot: deploy status: prototype cluster up in us-west-2 (relay-pt-01) — logs forwarded to #eng-logs.

 todd: tiny nit — name the project 'wg-tenant-relay' so it's searchable.

 priya: will do. tagging folks for review: @elaine @todd @mike — please add quick comments on RFC when I post. :thumbsup:
